content.title: About
content.content: Pumpkin is the fruit of a plant in the Cucurbitaceae family, cultivated in many regions worldwide. It has a mildly sweet flavor, soft flesh, and a hard rind. Pumpkin is used in cooking, baking, soups, and its seeds are also consumed.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Pumpkin is a symbol of autumn and Halloween in many countries.
There are over 200 varieties of pumpkin, differing in shape, size, and rind color.
Pumpkin seeds are rich in zinc and magnesium.
Pumpkin contains beta‑carotene, which the body converts to vitamin A.
Pumpkin can be used to make candles and decorative items.

items.title: Rich in beta‑carotene
items.content: Beta‑carotene in pumpkin converts to vitamin A, supporting vision and immune function.

items.title: Low in calories
items.content: Pumpkin is low in calories, making it suitable for weight‑management diets.

items.title: Source of dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion and promotes a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Antioxidants such as vitamin C and polyphenols help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Supports heart health
items.content: Potassium and magnesium in pumpkin help maintain normal blood pressure.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to pumpkin or its seeds.

items.title: Added sugar in processed products
items.content: Pumpkin in canned or sweetened forms may contain added sugars.

items.title: Digestive discomfort if overconsumed
items.content: Large amounts of pumpkin can cause gas and stomach discomfort.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Pumpkin can be roasted, boiled, steamed, used in soups, stews, pies, and desserts. Pumpkin seeds are roasted and eaten as a snack. Young pumpkin (summer squash) is often eaten raw in salads.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store whole pumpkins in a cool, dry, dark place for up to 2–3 months. Cut pumpkin should be kept in an airtight container in the refrigerator for 3–5 days. Frozen pumpkin can be stored for up to 6 months.
